prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation by heterobifunctional small molecules that recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation replaces occupancy-based inhibition with event-driven, catalytic removal of a chosen protein through a designed small molecule. The principle is molecular design in a strict sense: ligand and linker choice, ternary-complex cooperativity and E3 ligase selection can be tuned rationally. It changed what chemists and clinicians can attempt, because targets with no tractable active site can now be reached. Many laboratories confirmed the mechanism independently, and degraders are in the clinic. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the PROTAC concept, and Ciulli supplied the structure-based VHL ligands and the ternary-complex design rules that made the approach general. That makes a coherent three-person prize on one achievement.
statement.case_against: No bifunctional degrader has yet reached the clinical validation that sotorasib or an approved base-editing therapy would give, so the prize could be seen as early. The thalidomide-cereblon glue mechanism (Handa, Ito, Gray) is a separate and arguably more clinically advanced strand, and a PROTAC-only citation leaves it unrecognized. A fair prize may need a different configuration than the three names I propose.

responses.point: Linke ranks base editing (B061) first as a clear chemical principle with very large generative potential, already in clinical use, with Liu, Komor and Gaudelli as laureates.
responses.response: I agree base editing is a strong and clean chemical invention and I rank it highly. My reservation is attribution and proximity to the 2020 prize. Giving Komor and Gaudelli a prize as lead experimentalists would be unusual, and Liu alone is the more defensible configuration, so the three-person form you propose is less secure than it looks. The 2020 prize also covered the Cas9 platform, so the novelty argument is a little weaker than for degradation. I would place B061 as my first alternative, not my lead.

responses.point: Somfai ranks Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling first and ranks PROTACs fourth with the Crews, Ciulli, Deshaies trio, noting that the molecular glue strand is separate and may need its own recognition.
responses.response: I agree that the PROTAC trio is the clean core and the glue strand is a separate stream. I disagree that this argues for delay, because the concept is already mechanistically validated across many groups. On your first choice, C-N coupling is a fine and mature bond-forming method, but the 2010 cross-coupling prize and the 2021 organocatalysis prize leave synthetic methodology well represented. I do not see a comparable gap in the prize record for induced-proximity pharmacology. I do accept that your point on C-N coupling being overdue is serious, and I would not oppose it as an alternative.

responses.point: Chabes ranks base editing first and PROTACs third, but replaces Ciulli with Handa because Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target and so explains molecular glues.
responses.response: Replacing Ciulli with Handa is a serious option, and I treat it as unresolved. Handa's cereblon discovery gave the mechanistic explanation for glue degraders. But Crews, Deshaies and Handa would credit the idea and the molecular target, while omitting the structure-guided design rules, such as VHL ligands and ternary-complex cooperativity, that made degraders a programmable chemical tool. I keep Ciulli because the prize rationale I care about is design principles, but I would want the committee to test this choice directly.

responses.point: Aqvist puts Car-Parrinello dynamics first and ranks PROTACs third, saying the chemistry is solid but that no degrader is an approved drug yet, which argues for waiting.
responses.response: I take the maturity point seriously. The Car-Parrinello method has four decades of validation and I do not dispute that it is a game-changer. But the Nobel criterion is a discovery of great benefit, not an approved drug count. The PROTAC mechanism is confirmed, human proof of concept exists, and the principle will stand whether any particular molecule is approved. I would still rank the method well, but I do not think it displaces B028 on timing alone.

responses.point: Sparr ranks biomolecular condensates first as a physical-chemical principle of cellular organisation, with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen.
responses.response: The condensate work is a major conceptual change and I rank it third. My concern is that the physiological generality is still debated, and some in-cell claims have been challenged. Compared with degradation, the field has less settled evidence on what is truly liquid-liquid phase separation, and what clinicians can do with it differs. I would support revisiting it in a few years when that debate has narrowed.

uncertainties: Whether a PROTAC-focused citation should include a glue-degrader pioneer such as Handa or Gray, and which of Ciulli or Handa the committee prefers for the third place.
Whether the lack of an approved PROTAC drug makes recognition premature compared with base editing, which has patients treated.
I have not independently verified priority details or the latest clinical data on degraders.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my provided profile. I have no connection to any shortlisted candidate. My postdoc mentors (Molly Stevens, Freddy Boey) are not credited on any shortlisted ballot, and I work in sensor science and biomaterials, not degraders.
